_comment: Chapter 07's calls (least privilege for service principals), with the least-privileged Microsoft Graph permission or Azure role from the Learn page for each call, read on October 30, 2026. Same schema as calls.json; kept in its own file so chapters written in parallel don't collide. A task may make only its own calls. tests/NpiLeastPrivilege.Tests.ps1 fails when a task's declaration isn't exactly the union of its calls, or when the read task declares anything but GET.

calls.note: The application permissions a client service principal holds, on every resource, not only Microsoft Graph. The writer re-reads it before each removal.
Learn names Directory.Read.All as least privileged; the same read Chapter 01 makes tenant-wide, made here for one client at a time.
Each resource service principal once, for its appRoles and oauth2PermissionScopes, so app role IDs become permission names.
Filtered on principalId, one service principal at a time. A service principal in any directory role is handed to the Privileged Access plan (A3.4).
With $filter=assignedTo('{objectId}') for each managed identity, at each scope in azure-scopes.csv. Reader includes Microsoft.Authorization/*/read.
Each role definition once, so a role assignment's roleDefinitionId becomes a role name.

Removes one app role assignment through the RESOURCE service principal, as Learn recommends. Never deletes a service principal or an application. Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged role Learn lists for Microsoft Graph app roles; Application.ReadWrite.All doesn't manage app role assignments exposed by Microsoft Graph.

allowedBody.scope: a non-empty subset of the grant's current scopes

calls.note: Narrows a delegated grant's scope. The body overwrites the scope list, so the writer sends the whole kept list and nothing else.
